messages:
anya: starting a canary for Mekong13b v1.0 (int4) on dedicated nodes — noticed a few worker OOMs during longer conversations, trying to triage. anyone free?

devon: saw that on one run earlier. spikes after ~1200 tokens generated, even though active seq length was ~3000. memory usage jumps.

sasha: do we have max_new_tokens set high in the canary? what batch size?

anya: default canary config: `batch_size: 8`, `max_new_tokens: 1024`, `prefetch_kv: true`, `kv_cache_window: 4096`. running on p4d-like machines.

priya: can you paste the OOM log snippet?

anya: sure — log tail: ```
[2026-03-19T15:12:03Z] worker-12 ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
Model: Mekong13b-v1-int4, seq=4096, new_tokens=980, batch=8
KV cache bytes before gen: 5.2GB, after attempt: 7.9GB
Stack: serving/runtime/kv_cache.cpp:line 214
```

devon: that KV jump looks suspicious — maybe prefetch is duplicating KV for shards. Mekong's attention layout does per-head packing and our int4 kernels might allocate temporary buffers.

sasha: canary uses per-shard prefetch; try `prefetch_kv: false` and see if the OOM goes away. also try reducing batch_size to 4 as sanity.

anya: rolling a quick patch to the canary config now. will flip prefetch off and lower batch.

infra-bot: deploy patch mekong-canary/config@canary-20260319 applied to 3/3 hosts — rolling restart initiated.

anya: after change: batch=4, prefetch_kv=false — first two runs passed, then a solo OOM on a 1-of-8 concurrent request with long system prompt.

priya: can you dump allocator stats? Fragmentation metric would help (free_blocks vs total_allocated).

anya: allocator dump: `total_alloc=10.4GB, free=1.1GB, largest_free_block=120MB, num_free_blocks=42`

devon: fragmented. largest_free_block too small for our temporary int4 unpack buffer. looks like repeated allocations of small pieces during startup cause holes.

sasha: two mitigation ideas: 1) warmup allocation that reserves a contiguous temp buffer on startup, 2) bump default `max_new_tokens` to 512 for canary and enforce a per-request token cap until we fix allocator.

priya: also consider changing kernel path to in-place int4 path (less temporary memory) for Mekong until we upstream better alloc logic. tradeoff is slight latency increase.

anya: running a config with `max_new_tokens:512` + warmup reserve 1GB contiguous buffer + batch=4. will run eval suite after a couple hundred requests.

eval-bot: scheduled regression eval: 200 prompts (chat style) queued against Mekong13b-v1-int4 canary (config id canary-20260319-2).

infra-bot: canary hosts report warmup success: reserved 1.0GB contiguous temp buffer on each host.

anya: after 2 hours: no OOMs observed across 5k inferences. memory fragmentation metrics: `total_alloc=10.2GB, free=1.9GB, largest_free_block=980MB, num_free_blocks=9`

devon: great — warmup reserve fixed the fragmentation symptom. what's the eval result?

eval-bot: results in: metrics summary (int4 canary vs fp16 baseline):
- answer-match: int4 93.1% vs fp16 96.3% (delta -3.2%)
- perplexity (LM test): int4 29.4 vs fp16 27.8
- average latency p50: int4 220ms vs fp16 195ms
- tail errors: int4 0.4% bad_tokens vs fp16 0.1%

priya: 3.2% drop on answer-match is non-trivial. is that across all prompt types or concentrated?

eval-bot: concentrated in multi-step reasoning prompts and numeric extraction. simple chit-chat unaffected.

sasha: sounds like quantization introduced brittle numeric handling. try `per-channel-scale` for weight quant or apply bias-correction post-quant. also check layernorm fp32 fallback for sensitive layers.

anya: I can re-run a variant: int4-perchannel + layernorm-fp32 fallback + same warmup reserve. will queue as canary-3.

devon: also add canary-level QA: add regression prompts focused on numeric precision and multi-step chain-of-thought to our eval harness.

anya: queued. running now.

eval-bot: canary-3 run complete: answer-match 95.8% (delta -0.5%), perplexity 28.0, latency +10ms.

priya: good improvement. tradeoffs look acceptable for canary; still want to fix allocator long-term rather than rely on reserve.

sasha: file a follow-up ticket for allocator compaction and temp-buffer reuse in runtime; tag eng-runtime and eng-ml. also propose default server-side `max_new_tokens=512` for public hosted rollout unless customer overrides.

anya: filing ticket now: https://rwd.atlassian.com/browse/ML-8721 — includes reproducible script, allocator dump, and eval diffs.

devon: for Dedicated offering, recommend exposing a deploy knob `reserve_temp_buffer_bytes` so enterprise customers can opt-in while we fix runtime.

anya: noted. thanks all — will keep canary running with per-channel int4 + layernorm-fp32 fallback and monitor. :thumbsup:
